subject: Designing and auditing the multi-graph context architecture of an AI-coding workspace: skill graph, document routing…

evals.prompt: Define context-graph in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the context-graph skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind context-graph. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "scaffold a new SKILL.md from a template". Should context-graph activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force context-graph onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to skill-router, skill-infrastructure, skill-scaffold, knowledge-modeling, refactor, context-management, context-window, project-knowledge-extraction.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "we have ~300 skills but the agent never finds half of them — what's the diagnostic frame?". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying context-graph.

Place context-graph among its adjacent skills (skill-router, skill-infrastructure, skill-scaffold, knowledge-modeling, refactor, context-management, context-window, project-knowledge-extraction). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about context-graph and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
